reviews.text: 开始还好好的，玩到后边特效还有木头多了之后10分钟卡死一次，优化实在是有待提高

A very pleasant ride from start to finish. I will say, it took me a bit longer than it should have to find what the "meta" was to upgrades for each run. To me, this was a fresh twist on the "Do a run, upgrade, repeat" style because of the level up bonuses resetting between each run. That was irksome in it's own regard, because it felt bad to end a good run, but a good run signified a lot of upgrade progress, usually. Things did tick a little slowly in the end-game area with unlocking potions. Not to the point where I wasn't having fun, but it was enough for me to notice that things weren't going as smoothly as before. All in all, very enjoyable incremental game. A decent amount of time behind it (my hours are probably a little inflated due to me playing this secondary to other things I was doing. I'd say cut 2 hours off my time for true 100% time). Upgrades give the player good agency, and all the goals and requirements to unlock things felt pretty reasonable the whole way through. Thoroughly enjoyed my time here, and would love to see the dev make more games in the genre in the future.

I've unfortunately had about 10 crashes already in like 5 hours of play. The game also seems to be very near the end. While I liked it, I would've liked more game and fewer crashes I guess. Later edit: after switching off the 'floating damage numbers' option in settings, the crashes subsided and I could finish the game. While I still maintain it'd be nice to have a bit more content, it's a fun distraction and I would recommend it if you're looking for 4-5 hours of a semi-idle roguelite.

I'd say the game (after the hot fix) is okay. Not great, not good but something you pay a little to support the developer and enjoy a few hours of numbers going up. Early game (1-3 hours) as a player you'll feel like you are making incremental progress. But beyond that it becomes a real grind session to that feels like getting anywhere comes down to luck. Calling this an idle game feels disingenuous- there's an option in settings for upgrades to be selected automatically but otherwise there's too much need for keyboard interaction to move around and collect resources and mouse clicking to continue (could implement a timer to begin a 'New Run' or include a skill for auto 'New Run'). It has been mentioned that the need for both keyboard and mouse is a limitation that could be looked at: being able to select upgrades, skills and being able to continue with keyboard inputs would be a nice QOL nit-pick. Re-playable? As of 1.0.5 There's no way to start over nor a New Game+ mechanic so single play-through only. Things I would like to see that would make this a better game: Better stat descriptions. Further development of the skill tree for mid/late-game wood and gold sinks that address the grind. Indicators for 'Extended Cut' and 'Gravitation Pull' Ranges. 'Banned' upgrade pulls. A skill that increases the time gold/logs remain on screen? A New Game+ option

Finished the game just for the sake of getting my money's worth, but I would NOT recommend buying it. The largest glaring issue is the undisclosed AI assets, which is incredibly disgusting, but on top of that, the game itself has very poor balance and pacing. It slows down incredibly hard after a couple of hours and is just overall not very satisfying. Also, the combination of an idle/clicker plus a roguelike seems interesting on paper, but what it essentially boils down to is just always re-rolling for the same upgrades every run since nothing else even comes close to the same level of efficiency. TLDR: Feels quite rushed and unpolished, and also BOOO AI

Overall could’ve been a lot better. It started out fun, and satisfying seeing all the logs fly around while your drones scoop them up, especially when the “special logs” go off. But about halfway through I felt annoyed and ended up beating it just to beat it. Progression completely slows down unless you know the most optimal cards. You’d think increasing log value would actually matter so you can get more upgrades, but no— just stack damage over everything else. That defeats the purpose of the “rogue lite mechanics” when there’s such a strong meta build. Some runs feel like a waste of time and you might as well restart if you don’t get the right cards early on. Some sort of “Banish” skill would’ve helped here. I did like the different axes, lumberjacks, and customization options, but they didn’t feel like they mattered as much as the meta build. I also wish the UI used different colors, it was difficult to tell what was maxed without double checking. I also had a few times where upgrades didn’t save after relaunching the game. I’d save the $6.50 for something else.

It's an okay game. I do wish steam had "mixed" as a review option. My biggest gripe is it's in the idler category, and in the 2 hours i've played so far, there is no idling at all. It is very active incremental gameplay, which is fine, but every second or 2 there is a popup where you need to choose a perk or reroll, that pop up kills the game flow for me big time. It actually becomes annoying and i wish there was a way to just turn it off and just take less rewards and play for longer. The same upgrades all the time that only last the short run time you have, it's just a thorn in an otherwise pretty fun game. Chop, choose a perk, chop, choose another perk, chop chop, another perk, drone collects some wood, another perk. It's just mechanic spam.

An absolutely SPLENDID incremental game! Timber Rush has a fantastic visual style, is very well optimised and rarely drops any frames even with the utter chaos of logs and text popups on screen. The graphics style is gorgeous and the gameplay is hectic. My only complaint was it was a tad grindy for that final unlock and sometimes some runs felt poor where as other runs felt super overpowered (got 5000q on my final run) Besides that this is a SOLID game, well worth picking up and playing! :) I hope to see more incremental games match this quality! Great job, Allerton Apps! :D

An interesting blend of two genres. I think the pacing is a little bit frustrating, but it's a short enough experience that it's not a major nuisance. If you like the incremental genre, this is an easy choice to try. It also eventually becomes an idle game out of sheer brute power, which is always a funny thing to do in these types of games.

I want to say I would recommend this, because the core loop is pretty alright. The problem is that there's no AI disclaimer. When you actually get into the game, the visuals don't look as clean as they do on the storepage, and instead have that telltale AI look to them. Pixelart that just doesn't quite look right. Animations that look just look off, like no pixel artist would ever animate like this. It was either a case of GenAI being used to generate the assets, or they're intentionally trying to use an artstyle that is reminiscient of AI for whatever reason.

Game completed in about 11 hours (i have few hours in AFK tho). I wished there was more to the game. More complex modifiers and upgrades. Skill tree, crew and axes were all underwhelming and bit too simple. Also the ingame card system should have "banish" options for cards you do not want. At end there was more than half cards that are ZERO uses or help. Last push was done just by stacking chopping power +chopping speed + crit + crit power. Game is not worth the 4€ price pool as there is no reborn system / ascenssion or anything else after reacing 1 quadrillion logs. I also collected way more gold coins that had ZERO uses after upgrading all axes.
